A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the glycaemia and glycaemic index are not related in the type I diabetes, but the prandial glycosuria is.
the glycaemia and prandial insulin therapy in type 1 diabetic patients on CSII are not influenced by the GI of dietary carbohydrates.
the glycaemix index of the carbohydrate in the diet is not an important factor for the achievement of near-normal blood glucose concentrations in type I diabetic patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the glycaemia index can be helpful for the prediction, but not the control, of prandial glyco- and insulin levels in type I diabetes.
the glycaemia of a meal can be predicted with reasonable accuracy from the glycaemic response to a standard meal.
the glycaemia index of dietary carbohydrates can be useful for the individual prediction of insulin requirements.
